title: Hybrid hard/soft GPU tenancy: burstable micro-slices, eviction scoring, and autoscale backpressure
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem: Customers on Dedicated capacity sometimes suffer transient tail-latency spikes when other tenants burst; existing approaches (hard slicing or purely statistical throttles) either waste capacity or allow noisy neighbors to degrade SLOs. Proposal: implement a hybrid hard/soft tenancy model that combines small guaranteed GPU micro-slices with a reclaimable burst pool, an eviction-scoring mechanism for graceful soft-eviction, and autoscale backpressure signals that integrate with Dedicated autoscaler policies.
acceptance_criteria: Provide per-tenant guaranteed micro-slice (vGPU-like) with configurable baseline throughput expressed as tokens/sec or qps per GPU unit
Implement a shared burst pool that tenants can draw from when idle capacity exists; bursts are accounted as 'burst tickets' and have time-limited grants

Eviction scoring engine picks candidates for soft reclaim based on age of burst, historical SLA compliance, and model criticality label; evictions are signaled with a 500-1000ms graceful draining window
Autoscaler consumes backpressure telemetry (admission_reject_rate, eviction_pressure, kv-cache-hit-drop) and reduces scale-to-zero/hyper-scale triggers to avoid cascading impact
Instrument end-to-end SLO dashboards showing per-tenant p50/p95/p99 latency, burst-usage, reclaimed tokens, and customer-visible throttles
Regression tests and chaos experiments demonstrate <=2% p99 regression for guaranteed tenants when full burst pool is in use on a 100-node test fleet
